root_cause: inviteByNpub fetched the invitee's KeyPackage (443/30443) from the inviter's NDK pool only and never read the invitee's advertised relay list (kind 30051 d=marmot, or 10051), so a KeyPackage held only on advertised non-pool relays yielded no_key_package. NdkNetworkAdapter.getUserInboxRelays read kind 10051 only (the app publishes 30051) and, when it found a list, returned the listed relays alone, so the Welcome never went to the inviter's own relays alongside them.
fix: inviteeKeyPackageLookup.ts: parseInviteeRelayList (30051 d=marmot preferred, else 10051; invitee-authored AND signature-verified only; newest; wss:// or ws:// on localhost; no credentials; normalised, deduped, cap 3; total) and lookupInviteeKeyPackages (pool KeyPackage fetch and relay-list fetch start together; KeyPackage REQ to listed relays not covered by pool/effective relays over raw one-shot sockets with a 5 s bound, non-fatal; usable events = right kind, invitee-authored, verified; no_key_package/timeout semantics; NO NDK pool side effect). relayRequest.ts: requestRelayOnce (injected WebSocket ctor) and verifyRelayEvent. inviteByNpub delegates with real deps. getUserInboxRelays uses the verified parser, returns listed + effective relays (deduped, listed first), effective alone on no list/timeout/error. groups.md updated.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: NDK pool keys are normalised with a trailing slash while listed URLs are not, so pool membership and removal needed a normalised comparison, and removal must use the pool's own key. isValidRelayUrl is case-sensitive on the scheme, so scheme lowercasing must precede it. Round 1: the first design leaned on NDKRelaySet.fromRelayUrls, whose pool side effects (shared temporary relays, a 30 s removal timer) cannot be cleaned up safely; raw one-shot sockets removed the whole class of problem.
retrospective.surprised_by: NDKRelaySet.fromRelayUrls adds relays to the pool as a side effect, so the lookup had to snapshot the pool before and clean up after (finally) and settle both fetches before cleanup, or a still-running listed fetch could re-add a relay after removal.

remediation_note: Round 1 (findings A-F): listed relays are no longer put in the NDK pool (raw one-shot sockets via relayRequest.ts; pool snapshot/finally cleanup and poolRelayUrls/removePoolRelay deps deleted); every used event verified via injected verifyEvent (nostr-tools verifyEvent, existing dependency); listed-relay events also filtered to kind 443/30443 by the invitee; pool KeyPackage fetch started concurrently with the relay-list fetch; parser total; tests and docs corrected. Round 2: covered = permanentAndConnectedRelays only; getUserInboxRelays keeps a verified list received before a timeout; query kept in normalised URLs (fragment dropped); usable pool KeyPackage returned without awaiting listed relays; real-NDKEvent verifier test; docs corrected (Few's list preferred, newest of the chosen kind). Round 3: coverage snapshotted synchronously before the pool KeyPackage request (connect race); pool-key comparison tolerates NDK's trailing slash after a query; docs: only the key request is read from advertised relays and only it and the Welcome are sent, found-elsewhere wording for slow relays, own-relay copy used without comparison.
